txt: *teeth clattering*
A shaggy-looking girl in her late teens or early twenties kneels on the ice with an electronic contraption in her hand. Hearing you approach, she looks up.
Acele stares at him blankly. Two unflinching stares in collision course.
Acele using her contact mic to listen to a tree, underwater.
After a moment of silence she speaks again: "So, thanks. I guess. For the psych session. I guess that means we're... even?" She smiles a little.
After a moment of silence she speaks again: "So, thanks. I guess. For the psych session. Maybe I can return it -- what's been eating you, officer?"
Looking up she sees a grown man -- on the wrong side of forty, his face bloated from alcohol and god knows what else -- not so quietly crying.
She breathes on her fingers. Looks like she doesn't know what to say.
She gathers herself for a moment, then says, "Okay."
She looks back at her tape recorder.
She looks down, pretending to be busy with the device.
She looks up with a pained expression, her face caked with a thick layer of make up. With her left hand she's wiping some of it off to get the snow out of her face.
She looks up, not entirely sure what that means.
She looks you in the eye, her pupils wide, surrounded by a ridiculous amount of make-up.
She must be Acele, the last of the speedfreaks' 'posse'.
She nods, apprehensively.
She nods, very cautiously.
She shrugs, obviously eager to go back to whatever she's doing.
She's shivering a bit.
She's waiting.
Startled, she turns her head and looks at the sea. No modes of indirect taxation catch her eye. She looks back at you.
The girl looks down, slowly curling into a ball.
The girl stands behind the row of pulpits, whistling a melody with the electronic device pressed against the wood. At the sound of your footsteps, she stops what she was doing.
The shaggy-haired girl kneels on the sea ice. She looks up as you approach.
The wind howls. She remains silent.

The words are stuck in your throat. All that comes out is tears, pouring down your face. The young woman has kept her eyes trained on her wires, waiting for the lecture to end, but now she hears sobbing...
The young woman has kept her eyes trained on her wires, waiting for the sorry spectacle to end, but it's gone awful quiet up there. Then, the sound of sobbing...
The young woman lifts her headphones up slightly and raises her chin, looking at you expectantly.
"*Rich* people. Rich people are east of the river."
"*Why?*" She raises a brow.
"... but I shouldn't, really. I have stuff planned for tomorrow. Gotta run around, try to make some money."
"A 'SKULL thing'?" She shakes her head. "Man, you sound like a hundred years old when you say that."
"A city has millions in it, so the world would have a lot more. I think I knew the number once..."
"A contact mic is a microphone that records sounds from inside things. Like all this wood."
"A contact mic records sounds from inside things. Like this ice."
"A life full of suspicion. Perhaps you should talk to Noid, you'd get along nicely... Now, was there something else on your mind?"
"A shame you didn't..."
"Acele."
"Actually just one wire, I picked on it 'til the braiding came loose. The wire leads to a contact microphone."
"Actually just one wire, I picked on it till the braiding came loose. The wire leads to a contact microphone."
"Actually, we don't know where he's from. Or who he is, really."
"Ah! No. This is a *contact microphone*, it's for recording *inside* solid objects. Contact Mike just beats people up."
"All right," she concedes. "My father was a Zemylaki. He died years ago. He was a bad man. Not a lot of good things to say about him and what he did."
"Alright..." She smiles a little, without meaning to.
"Alright." She picks up the tape recorder and looks you in the eye...
"And no, it's got nothing to do with Contact Mike."
"And the crab-man hasn't shown himself much, thank god."
"And then, you know, right behind her a man *crawled down the wall*. Upside down, like a crab. Down the church wall. I think the woman didn't even know he was there, he was completely silent..."
"And yes, I'm being more like Contact Mike, alright. Don't even bring it up."
"Andre's overthinking it," says the girl with the microphone.
"Andre, pull the compressor! The place is gonna come down..."
"Andre? He's a cool guy. Doesn't really come off as one, but he is. To me at least..."

"Anodic music doesn't really do vocals in the traditional sense. Vocals are thought of as *rock*. That's to say they're a bit *backward*. No offence if you like rock music, though. Rock music is cool by me."
"Anything to get through." She shrugs. "That's how it is after the fall."
"Anyway, I thought I'd make some, too. It's supposed to be, like, a music place anyway..." She rubs her shoulders and looks around.
"Anyway, even if you don't have vocals you still need someone to say something every now and then, right? To urge things on. That's where the party boy comes in..."
"Anyway…" She turns back to you. "Shot in the leg... I'm sorry, man, that must suck."
"Aren't they?" She seems perplexed. "I thought they were as *Vacholiere* as any of us, just way richer."
"Beats me... Noid said they get along, somehow. They're both crazy enough, I guess."
"Beats me." She exhales a puff of shimmering cold air. A moment passes.
"Beautiful..."
"Because... Listen, man, why does anyone do anything?"
"Believe me, dude, it's better we talk about something else."
"Bet they like it that way," she mutters. Quietly, under her breath.
"But *Disco* Elysium..." She looks unsure. "Isn't it wacky? Disco's kind of gone, isn't it? Forgotten."

"But earlier today she told me about... welkins?" Acele grimaces, as if it's the first time hearing the word. "And she seemed oddly happy. Like she had had some idea with those... little creatures. Some artistic idea. I didn't really listen, I was busy with my mic."
"But that's not really what I wanted to talk about. I wanted to thank you instead."
"C'mon, I can tell." She shakes her head slowly. "But, okay, be a boiadeiro about it if you want to."
"C'mon, man. Don't be like that. I mean, maybe she did, but you don't know that."
"C'mon, man. Don't mess around..." She hesitates.
"C'mon, man. We're in it. This is North Jamrock -- Martinaise. Sort of. The technicalities are confusing."
"C'mon, quit playin'. Will you help us with the church?"
"Come on, Noid. I think we owe him."
"Come to think of it, yes!" She laughs.
"Contact mics," she repeats, turning the device in her hand.
"Crying helps, though. Get it out of your system and then maybe we can talk, okay? I'll be here."
"Damn it's cold outside..."
"Diamorphine? But that hasn't been around for years -- five or more, like, seven years maybe? Everybody just does *hunch* now."
"Do. It's for the best."
"Doesn't hurt to ask, I guess..." She shrugs.
"Don't know what makes you think it'll be any different later, but..."
"Egg came with us. He made this wheezing puppy dog sound all the way back. Couldn't even speak."

"Egg was yelling along to some jams someone was spinning, all night long. Just kept yelling until he didn't have a shred of voice left. When the sun came up over the mines... there were mines? Yeah, it was in Coal City!" She nods.
"Exactly. It's our chance to turn the grim desolation into an overwhelmingly fun dance party!"
"Except that... yeah." She looks at the old wooden church up on the poles. As a mean wind comes bellowing in, the six-story structure lets out a doleful shriek.
"Excuse me?" She casually brushes her hand through her hair.
"For getting me and my friends in here. And we even found some new... associates, such as they are."
"Gee, thanks. Now, was there anything else on your mind?"
"Go ahead..."
"Go ahead."
"Good for you then. Women's fencing *is* a pretty graceful sight."
"Good for you. Now, was there anything else on your mind?"
"Good luck crossing that river on your police salary then."
"Good luck, guys."

"Good, I think. Noid is getting a read on the place, I think he finds the carpentry very impressive. Andre's been setting up the compressor and... dancing. Egg Head's keeping the party up, he's got the stage under control."
"Good, so you believe me." She looks at the tent. "You should go tell this to Andre, he'll know what to do next."
"Great!" She shivers. "Let us know if there's any progress, will you? We've been waiting for weeks here."

"Guys, we can't do The Return. There are like tons of places called The Return already. There's this communist joint in Jamrock that my friends like to frequent, and then there's this really famous radio show, you know the one..."
"Hard-cop." She nods to you with respect and turns off her recording device.
"He abides by the hard core, sir. You would have to ask him yourself."
"He basically just stands on the stage and dances and yells how awesome everything is. It's very catchy."
"He bought the family a huge house, so we got to live... at least temporarily... in a giant *castle* in Jamrock. And then he died."
"He looked like a banger, okay? He was all muscular and stuff. Had a mesh tanktop. I know it sounds ridiculous, but that only made it scarier, in a way..."
"He stopped right before he got to the floor, then just hung there like that, looking at me. Right at me. I fucking turned around and walked out. End of story."
"He takes care of shit. Sorry, I mean he's got a *vision*. Of what life should be, you know? He tries to push things until everything falls into place. He's an organizer."
"He's a Faubourger I guess, like the rest of us. Okay, maybe not Egg, I don't know about him, but Noid and the rest are from Faubourg, making the pilgrimage up north to visit The Paliseum."
"He's a carpenter. Trained and all. He's very good, he just doesn't have the mindset to work like that -- in a shop somewhere."
"He's in some kind of a self-destruction mode with that hair of his. Bleaching it like that. Probably wants to get rid of it altogether."
"He's real hard core about the lifestyle."
"Hello again." The girl looks up at you for a moment before turning back to her work.
"Hey there." The girl with an electronic recording apparatus turns to you as you approach.
"Hey, remember how earlier I said I didn't *need* your help?"

"Hey, there." She gives you a shy smile. "I've been recording some new audio from all these beams and rafters. The sounds travelling through the wood are pretty cool -- creaks and stuff. Like you're underwater, you know... But, like, underwater inside a tree."
"Hey... don't get me wrong. But you're a *cop*, right..."
"Hey..." Acele looks up from her microphone. "What did you do to Egg Head, cop-man? Did you *break* him?"
"Hey..." Her black eyes widen. "You're a cop..."
"Hmm..." She looks eastward. "Maybe you're right. Most of them do speak three languages."
"Hmm..." She sits back on the blanket, ears red from cold. "That's odd. You should search her machine, maybe it says where she went?"
"How about something simple, like 'The Club'?"
"How about we *don't* do that, Noid?" Another voice. "She looks cool."
"How come you don't remember though? Is it, like, some *selective memory* thing?"
"How come you don't remember though? Is it, like, some selective memory thing?"
"Huh?" She looks up at you, distracted.
"Hunch is like ten times stronger than diamorphine and *waaay* more lethal. I think the name is... B-hydroxy-something."

"I *think* I'm recording cracks in the ice, but there's no way to tell. Not without headphones. I think I just recorded your footsteps, too. Not sure how that will sound..." She scratches her forehead.
"I can't believe this turned into another Mike thing... Fine, okay, I'll stick to it." She takes the device from you and places it in her lap. "I'll knock it out in three rounds."
"I did and I'm sorry." She doesn't appear surprised. "For what it's worth... which isn't much."
"I didn't mean to, I'm sorry..." The girl is visibly shaken.
"I don't blame you. I mean, I wouldn't believe me either. I'm surprised Noid did. Andre I expected, but Noid..." She shakes her head.
"I don't care, I don't like the crab-man and I don't like his ideas, his ideas are spooky. Next, please!"
"I don't know man, have you *been* down Boogie Street? It's a little bewildering."
"I don't know what that means either."
"I don't know, man... things. Just stuff you need for life."
"I don't know, some kind of a... store?" She pauses to think. "Maybe a general store... Look man, fuck the hat."
"I don't really know what I'm doing. They use synthesizers, too. I don't have a synthesizer."
"I got my recordings to do, I feel better outside..." A wave breaks close-by and covers her in a cold spray.
"I guess so." She hesitates. "Anyway -- what else?"
"I just try to stay away from the crab-man, but he talks to Noid. They seem to have some 'thing' going on."
"I know. But I knew you'd see through their plan too. I'm not an idiot. I should have been able to control them. I will in the future. I promise."
"I know. I should have been able to control them. And I will in the future. I promise."
"I know." Her teeth rattle. She takes the device from you and places it in her lap. "I'll stick to it."

"I know." She nods towards the sloping mass of wood on the coast, then shivers. "It's not my idea. Andre and the boys found the place. It was supposed to be deserted, but now they can't even take it..."
"I mean, not that he does drugs. Just *high* you know."
"I really wanted to say: thanks for getting me and my friends in here. And we even found some new... associates, such as they are."
"I swear to god, I will always wear a hat from now on."
"I took that into account, of course. Coordinated the operation with the Débardeurs, else they might get... unhappy."
"I was kinda hoping you'd end this mess, though. It feels like I've been turning dad-wise, into a corrupt business-person. I don't like it."
"I was wondering when you would come around. What's up?"
"I'll keep that in mind, for future use." She turns to check her tape recorder.
"I'll try."
"I'm a silver bird."
"I'm kinda hoping you'll end this mess before we get going... I feel as if I'm slowly turning dad-wise, into a corrupt business-person. I don't like it."
"I'm listening." A cold wind blows in from the sea. She breathes on her fingers for warmth, looking up at you.
"I'm listening." She puts the contact mic down and props herself up a bit, waiting for you to speak.
"I'm listening." She puts the device down and props herself up a bit, waiting for you to speak.
"I'm ready if you are, detective."
"I'm ready if you two are, detectives."
"I'm sorry I said 'fuck the hat.' I was concentrating on something else..."

"I'm sorry, sir. I'm sorry. I was trying to concentrate on this thing here and I'm sorry I said that. My dad swears, my boyfriend swears... my whole family does. I've caught the habit. I didn't mean to... and I'm sorry."
"I've never seen him so psyched about anything though -- and he's often psyched. Looked sort of desperate, like it's his last chance or something. Or maybe he was just high..."
"I, like, saw you go into the tent. It's right there."
"I... don't know what that means."
"Is there a law that would stop me from lying, though?"
"Is this a rhetorical question?"
"Is this about the hat again?" She looks up at you, distracted. "I don't see you wearing a hat..."
"It just means that even if I did do drugs, I would not do them with a person I just met." She looks confused.
"It means I don't answer questions about myself."
"It was a stupid idea and I'm still disappointed *I* came up with it."

"It was definitely Coal City, because it took us two days to walk back to the Fau. He just wheezed the whole way, we never really asked him why he came with us. Or who he was. I think his name is Germaine..."
"It was too dark." She shakes her head. "I couldn't tell exactly."
"It's Noid's padlock, for keeping creeps and weirdos out. You should probably talk to him about it."
"It's a good thing you ended that mess, though. I felt I was turning dad-wise, into a corrupt business-person. Unpleasant."
"It's a music club and a synthesizer workshop. On Boogie Street, in Jamrock. Musicians live there, like... real musicians. I once saw Arno van Eyck!"
"It's creaking really loud."
"It's just something poor Faubourg kids do every spring, to pass the time. We walk the entire length of Boogie Street, up to Jamrock. Or as much as possible."
"It's pretty desolate here, I only hear the dogs bark at night and see the shadows move down the coast."
"It's settled, then. Everyone, welcome to Disco Elysium!" A light beam washes over the dance floor, bathing it in violet blue.
"It's settled, then. Everyone, welcome to No Truce with the Furies!"
"It's supposed to become, like, a club. For *anodic dance music*. Like that new style of synthesizer stuff they play at The Paliseum."
"It's too long. No one's going to remember it on a Friday night."
"It's... it's not important, actually. Never mind, I actually wanted to thank you."
"Like what?
"Like what?" She straightens out slightly, propping herself up with her hands, waiting for you to speak.
"Like what?" She straightens out slightly, propping herself up with her hands.
"Like what?"
"Like... the I-can't-remember-the-name-of-the-club amnesia?"
"Man, I have no clue, either."
"Man, that's because my equipment's on the ground."
"Man, when I get hurt I just wanna forget that shit, you know? That kind of selective memory."
"Man, you are one weird cop."
"May I ask, what did you tell them?"
"Maybe you could *talk* to Andre and the guys? Because there are some strange things going on in that church... if you're police you should look into it, right?"
"Me? I'm a silver bird."
"Me?"
"Mhm..." She breathes on her fingers again to warm them. "Thought so."
"Much warmer in here."
"Music stuff mostly. Like this tape recorder, but bigger. And there's piles of it."
"Must have taken it as a sign when he found it abandoned like that. Said it was an *augury*. I don't know where he got that from." She smiles. "Andre's not super intelligent..."
"My 'associates'?" She blows on her chilled fingers. "I haven't got much to say about them."
"My boyfriend sold them."
"My dad was a drunk. Plus, I guess I just wanted to drink too, you know? Get my *party on*."
"My whole family swears and it rubbed off on me..." There's a pained expression on her face. She'll answer your questions now.

"Nah, to me it sounds like classic van Eyck, I don't think he needs any 'inspiration' from folk songs. Maybe he lives in Martinaise and just threw away a part of his song because he thought it wasn't good enough?"
"No man, fuck that, I'm cool... I'm sorry I said that. I'm sorry about the *fuck*."
"No, Egg! It's the window." The glass shards around Dolores Dei's vacant heart appear to be vibrating from the sound. It almost looks as if she's alive.
"No, it sounds like you've just got chick issues."
"No, man. Fuck it, I'm cool... I'm sorry I said that. I'm sorry about the *fuck*."
"No-no." She cuts you off before you can finish the sentence. "I actually wanted to thank you. For getting me and my friends in here. And we even found some new... associates, such as they are."
"No. Recording." She stares at you, then briskly shakes her head and puts her headphones back on.
"No. Recording." She turns to Soona, then back to you. She briskly shakes her head and puts her headphones back on.
"No."
"Not in person, but I let them know. You can't do anything without the fat ones getting wind. It wasn't too difficult to convince them, really..."
"Not really, no."
"Not to sound too dramatic, but I wouldn't make light of his belief system when he's around. Noid's a serious person. He's serious about the lifestyle."
"Nothing," she says. "Anyway -- what else?"
"Nothing. But then again... there's nothing to organize around here either. He really wants this church thing to work..."
"Now, uh... we were talking about my contact mic?" She picks up the device and inspects it, avoiding your eyes.
"Of course I do. I just don't tell people about my friends and who they are and so on. I don't provide information on them."
"Oh man, you haven't been to The Paliseum?" She forgets herself for a moment. "It's *the* coolest place in this whole drug-addled shithole."
"Oh yeah..." She looks you over, assessing your age. "Guess you wouldn't know van Eyck. Or really be a Paliseum-going kind of person... "
"Oh! Well, good for you."
"Oh!" She almost smiles, but then decides not to. There's a moment of silence.
"Oh, I didn't notice that."
"Oh, but I am."
"Oh, hello there."
"Oh, here we go..."
"Oh, of course." She doesn't look surprised.
"Oh, of course." She doesn't sound surprised.
"Oh, really?"
"Oh, right. That's wise." She nods. "Take your time."
"Oh, that... he's the party boy."
"Oh, that... you're not gonna believe me. There's no point in me telling you."
"Oh, the crab-man." She shudders. "Still gives me the creeps, the way he moves... But he doesn't actually come down that much, just climbs around the rafters."
"Oh, they are. And I'm scum."
"Oh, yeah. Egg's *really* into him. Maybe even *too* into him. He's a pretty intense personality."
"Oh. Okay." She sits back on the blanket, ears red from cold. "What about Andre? You should go talk to Andre if you don't want to talk to me."
"Okay then," she nods. "They certainly do around me."
"Okay then. That's cool."
"Okay, but I still regret it. I should have been able to control them. And I will in the future. I promise."
"Okay, bye." She turns her attention back to the recording device.
"Okay, if it floats your boat I'll be more like Contact Mike and less like me."
"Okay, of course... What did you want to know?"
"Okay, so you're not *that* upset, it sounds like."
"Okay, then you should go and take a look, I guess. Boogie Street is cool. It's got a lot of immigrants and all kinds of different people."
"Okay, well..." She hesitates. "Maybe you could *talk* to Andre and the guys? Because there are some strange things going on in that church... if you're police you should look into it, right?"
"Okay, what else?"
"Okay, why do you think that?"
"Okay," she nods. "I went in and saw a woman next to one of those machines there. Noid calls it a *mainframe*..."
"Okay... but you'll still let us know if you learn something about the church, right?" She rubs her sides. "We don't have anywhere else to go anyway."
"Okay... it's a huge ghetto just south of Jamrock."
"Okay..." She hesitates. "It's Berger."
"Okay." Her teeth rattle. She takes the device from you and places it in her lap. "I'll stick to it."
"Okay." She shrugs. "To each his own."
"Okay."
"Okey dokey then."
"Once or twice, yeah. I'm sorry I haven't had the *Revachol experience* they get east of the river."
"One time we were out partying, somewhere in backwater Faubourg. Or maybe even Coal City, I can't remember. Maybe it was Coal City..."
"Or it might just be psych bullshit, you know? Königstein wank."
"Or, or... I'm just gonna put this out there -- are you sure you're not having *chick* issues, with some chick?"
"Ouch." She looks at your leg. "I did notice you limping, but I thought maybe it was your 'thing' or something..."
"People are sweet," she says quietly.
"Real cool..." She looks down at the device, mumbling under her breath.
"Really?" She appears to believe you. "You seem pretty upset about this *chica*... are you sure you don't remember anything about her? Eyes? Hair colour?"
"Really?" She appears to believe you. "You seem pretty upset about this *chica*... are you sure you don't remember anything about her?"
"Recording the audio coming through the wooden framework. I bet it's pretty cool. Creaks and stuff. Sounds like when you're underwater, you know?"
"Recording, I guess."
"Right."
"Same place I got the recorder from. The Paliseum."
"See? That's the appropriate way to give a girl a hat..."
"She was dressed like someone who's being raised by their grandmother, you know. Strange old clothes. Had this absent expression, didn't say anything, just stood still."
"Shoot." A cold wind blows. She breathes on her hands for warmth.
"Sir," she gives you a switchblade smile. "I abide by *the law*."
"So after his death we had nothing left. And we were in danger. My mother had to change her name, mine too. We left it all behind."
"So should you."
"So you talked to my associates, right? Are you gonna help us? With the church, I mean."
"So, like..." The girl on the ice looks up at you. "Seriously, what's eating you, man?"
"So, the thing that's been eating you... is rich people not having enough money?"
"So, the thing that's been eating you... is the slow pace of social progress?"
"Soona, the programmer, she's doing... whatever she does, behind that radiocomputer of hers. She doesn't talk to us much. And the crab-man hasn't shown himself, thank god."
"Soooo...?" The young woman looks at you, then the lieutenant, then you again. Then at the shore. She seems uncomfortable.
"Sorry, I don't really want that." She looks away.
"Sorry, I have stuff planned for tomorrow. Gotta run around, try to make some money."
"Sorry, man. My mind was elsewhere." She puts the device down. "Shoot."
"Sorry, mister, I don't really do drugs. Especially with people I just met."
"Sorry. I just don't tell people about my friends and who they are and so on. I don't provide information on them."
"Sorry."
"Sorry?" She looks confused.
"Sounds like it's smiling."
"Sounds like money."
"Sucks, man." She squints her eyes for a second trying to remember something... then lets go of it. "Was there something else? About the contact mic, perhaps?"
"Superstition. We can turn the grim desolation into a fun dance club, and thus also help turn this hell-hole around."
"Sure. Contact mic." She nods, staring at the recording device in her hands.
"Sure..." she says, slightly disoriented. "What do you want to know?"
"Sure."
"Synthesizers and tape consoles, microcomputers too. Anything that uses electricity, but isn't guitars... also found sounds. Stuff like that."
"Take your time, I guess. We don't have anywhere else to go anyway."
"Thank you," the young woman says blithely. "I'll get them under wraps, I promise."
"Thank you." The young woman nods. "I'll get them under wraps, I promise."
"Thank you."
"Thanks for helping us out. My associates and I are settling in here nicely. Even found some new associates." She turns back to her work, whistling softly...
"Thanks." She puts it on. It's a bit large for her.
"That stuff is more expensive than I am. More expensive than any of us, really. Doesn't matter. I can take the cold."
"That's cool by me." She nods knowingly.
"That's cool." She breathes on her fingers. Looks like she doesn't know what to say.
"That's my name. I take it you have met the others. Did they tell you about the church and the club... thing?"
"That's not going to lead anywhere with Evrart. He'll just deny everything. I mean, have you seen the guy?"
"That's real cool. Hope you don't mind missing out on all that great homo-sexual content the world has got to offer."
"That." She nods toward the church. "The boys think it could be a *place*, like The Paliseum or something. Stupid. It's really..." she pauses, "not gonna be a Paliseum, that's for sure."
"The frequency can't be *that* low..."
"The mic? I don't exactly know. Somehow it doesn't pick up vibrations from the air. The box said it only picks up *structure-borne sound*. If you like technobabble."

"The musicians in The Paliseum use them for making music. They loop the stuff, cutting the tapes together. They make music out of cracks in the ice and keys jangling... crazy sounds like that. It's hard to explain."
"The usual. I had a shitty run as a teenager."
"Then you really haven't seen much of this *strange world*, because we literally haven't got any income taxes. Just a 20% value-added tax and that's, like... *it*."
"There is."
"There you have it then. Chick trouble. Who is she?"
"They do say death is an avenue. Like all the others." She's silent for a second like she's going to add something. But she doesn't.
"They got too much stuff crammed in there. No room."
"They're inside that thing there." She points to the tent. "Would be cool if you did... Was there something else?"
"Thirty minutes or so." She raises an amused eyebrow.
"This place must have a mind of its own..."
"This... isn't really about the hat, is it?"
"This?" She breathes on her freezing fingers. "It's a portable recording device. It's for field recording. Low quality, but still."
"This?" She taps on the electronic device. "Yeah, it's a portable recording device. For field recording. Low quality, but still."
"To keep more weirdos from getting in. Fucking Martinaise... I'm sorry." She rattles her teeth. "It's got the worst weirdos. If you get around to it, ask Andre about them, he'll tell you."
"Tsk..." She lets a quiet *tsk* roll off her tongue. "What kind of law says that?"
"Uh huh, and you're sure it's social progress you're distressed about and not, I don't know, some chick?"
